Why: Massive tubulin intensity/texture rise, bundling visuals, and 5/5 top atlas stabilizer matches support this MoA.

Next experiment if this were a real lab: In vitro tubulin polymerization assay plus phospho-histone H3 mitotic index and washout to confirm stabilized microtubules and mitotic arrest.

## PI review

Verdict: approve.

Clean separation on quantitative and orthogonal evidence. Both wells (dose 7/3uM and dose 5/0.3uM, rep1) show massive tubulin bundling directionality: tub_glcm_contrast z+122/+155, tub_std z+70/+77, tub_mean z+39/+42, with loss of nuclear regularity (nuc_solidity -40/-29). This is the opposite direction from Microtubule destabilizers (tubulin loss) and primary Actin disruptors, and far exceeds the secondary mitotic signal expected from Eg5/Aurora inhibitors. The phenotype read on both wells directly reports thick bright tubulin bundles/rings in rounded mitotic-like cells, matching the quantified texture rise, not merely a generic mitotic arrest. Atlas agreement is decisive: the 5 nearest neighbours are all Microtubule stabilizers at similarity 0.93-0.97, while the runner-up Protein degradation neighbours are only 2/10 at lower similarity (0.84-0.85), so the runner-up cannot explain the tubulin-dominant profile equally well. The dose pairing was discriminative and the two independent wells act as cross-dose replication, so this is not a single-well or weak-effect call (n=137 and 230 cells, z>100 effects). The 0.94 probability is appropriately tempered for single-replicate wells. Budget is exhausted and the concordant profile + visual + atlas lines leave no affordable orthogonal test that would plausibly move the call. Concur with Microtubule stabilizers at 0.94.

## Unblinding

Compound: **epothilone B** (PubChem CID [448013](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/448013))

Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree

ChEMBL mechanisms: Tubulin stabiliser

## Verdict (computed by code)

Correct: agent said **Microtubule stabilizers**, BBBC021 annotates **Microtubule stabilizers**.

## Reflection

The call was driven by concordant quantitative, visual and atlas evidence. Acquiring the highest dose first then a mid-high dose gave cross-dose replication: both wells showed extreme tubulin texture and intensity increases with loss of nuclear regularity, and the microscopist directly reported thick bright bundles/rings rather than generic mitotic arrest, which matched the 5 nearest atlas neighbours all being Microtubule stabilizers at high similarity.
The main risks were over-reading generic signals and limited sampling. Nuclear solidity loss alone is shared with Eg5 and other mitotic MoAs, and the atlas contained Protein degradation and Cholesterol-lowering neighbours at lower similarity that were not orthogonally tested. Tempering to 0.94 was appropriate because both wells were single replicates and no low-dose threshold well was acquired.
Unblinding as epothilone B with Tubulin stabiliser annotation confirmed the directionality logic: increased tubulin intensity and contrast indicating bundling is opposite to destabilizers and exceeds secondary mitotic effects, supporting continued reliance on tubulin-dominant texture plus visual bundling plus atlas agreement for this MoA.

What was right:
- Massive tubulin texture/intensity rise in both wells correctly indicated stabilization/bundling rather than destabilizer loss
- Visual report of thick bright tubulin bundles/rings in rounded cells correctly confirmed the quantified contrast/std increase
- Atlas comparison correctly prioritized 5/10 Microtubule stabilizer neighbours at 0.93-0.97 over lower-similarity Protein degradation runner-up

What was wrong or missed:
- Did not acquire low-dose wells so missed onset/threshold and relied on only two high-dose single-replicate wells
- Retained small residual probability for Protein degradation from 2/10 atlas neighbours without an orthogonal exclusion test
- Nuclear solidity loss is generic mitotic irregularity and would have been misleading if weighted without the tubulin-dominant signal and visuals

Proposed next experiment: Cell-free tubulin polymerization assay with epothilone B vs DMSO and paclitaxel control, plus washout and phospho-histone H3 mitotic index in cells to confirm stabilized polymers and mitotic arrest.
